faqs.q: How often should I go to the dentist for a check-up?
faqs.a: Many dentists suggest a routine check-up about every six months, but the right gap depends on your oral health, so your dentist may advise more or less frequent visits. Go even when nothing hurts, because cavities and gum disease often cause no symptoms in the early stages.

faqs.q: Should I use a soft or hard toothbrush?
faqs.a: A soft-bristled toothbrush is recommended for most people. Hard bristles and heavy pressure can wear down enamel and irritate the gums, so brush gently for about two minutes twice a day, making sure you clean every surface of your teeth.

faqs.q: Is it safe to whiten teeth at home?
faqs.a: Home whitening products can work, but overusing them or using them without guidance can cause tooth sensitivity and gum irritation. It is safer to have a dentist check your teeth first and recommend a suitable method, whether whitening in the clinic or a home kit used under their supervision.

faqs.q: Can a cavity heal on its own?
faqs.a: No, once decay has made a hole in the tooth it cannot heal by itself and usually needs a filling. Very early weakening of the enamel, before a hole forms, can sometimes be reversed with fluoride and good brushing, which is why regular check-ups that catch decay early are useful.
